analysis:
The examined units are test golden layout fixtures under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/PlacementChecks/Golden/layouts/. These are gemma-4-26b-8bit.json head line 1 and gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit.json base and head line 1. The gemma-4-26b.json unit is metadata only; its patch excerpt shows a single-line change of the same kind.

In each fixture, generationModes changes from [pipeline_v1] to [pipeline_v1, tensor_parallel_v1]. The fixtures also gain a routedExperts block and a tensorParallel layout block. That block has ranks=2, reduction sealed_all_gather_sum_v1, partialsDType float32 and shardRule kernel_aligned_heads_and_channels_v1. artifactSHA256 and configurationSHA256 are unchanged, and so are the per-layer weights.

These are test expectations, not runtime policy. No production gate, crypto, attestation, authorization or cache code appears in this batch.

One integration question remains. The fixtures imply that a new tensor_parallel_v1 cluster mode has been added elsewhere in the PR. In that mode, per-layer partial activations (float32, about 101 KB per token) are exchanged between ranks via sealed_all_gather_sum_v1. These partials are derived from consumer prompts (A-001) and cross provider or cluster boundaries (TB-002, TB-007). The integration pass should verify the following:
- The sealing of all-gather partials: AEAD, key binding per request and per rank, and replay or ordering protection.
- That rank peers are attested and authorized under TB-011 and T-053.
- That admission enforces the memory charges (requestChargeEveryRankBytes) to avoid DoS.
- That sharded state does not interact with SSD prefix-cache scoping (T-041, cacheSalt).

This source is not supplied here, so no finding is made on that path.
